Subject: Concordance checklist: MAP + evaluation exit criteria (CareQuest)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attached is an initial Mutual Action Plan workbook (MAP_v1.xlsx) plus a one-page SLA rollup. I wanted to capture a concise concordance checklist so everyone is aligned on what "success" looks like for the pilot and the gating conditions for a production decision. High level below — please review and flag anything missing: 

Top-line success criteria (what CareQuest needs to see):
- Precision target: >= 92% correct routing on the 3 primary intents in a 1,000-sample blind test (see Acceptance Test A).
- Latency SLO: P95 inference latency <= 180 ms for 2k token context under dedicated pool.
- Cost envelope: projected token cost <= $0.0025/token at target throughput (per MAP workbook).
- Privacy/Compliance: all logs encrypted and retained per your retention policy (30 days initial; longer-term optional).

Exit gates (conditions that must be true to move to next phase):
1) Functional: Acceptance Test A and B pass (detailed below).
2) Ops: Dedicated capacity reserved and smoke-run successful (1 week).
3) Security: SOC2 self-attestation and completion of questionnaire items 4–7.
4) Commercial: PO for Reserved Capacity or written approval to move to paid hosted plan.

Acceptance tests (what we will run):
- Acceptance Test A — Blind concordance: CareQuest provides 1,000 anonymized samples. Redwood runs inference; metrics computed: intent accuracy, top-2 coverage, false positive rate. Pass if intent accuracy >= 92% and top-2 coverage >= 97%.
- Acceptance Test B — Latency & throughput smoke: Run 2k-context sequences at target throughput for 24 hours. Pass if P95 <= 180 ms and no more than 1% error rate.
- Acceptance Test C — Regression sample: 200 edge-case prompts flagged by CareQuest (handled within 72 hours with documented mitigation).

Proposed timeline (we can compress if you want):
- Week 0 (this week): agree MAP workbook, identify sample owners, sign NDA amendment for sample export.
- Week 1–2: sample transfer + initial model tuning.
- Week 3: Acceptance Test A (blind run).
- Week 4: Acceptance Test B (24h smoke) + ops runbook verification.
- Week 5: Decision & PO / next-phase sign-off.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (worksheets: milestones, owners, sample inventory), SLA_Rollup.pdf (SLOs / fallback policies).

Next steps: please confirm the sample delivery owner and whether Procurement should be looped in now or at sign-off. Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the workbook.

—
Marissa Cole

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick read. Short answers inline and added operational fallbacks below. 

1) Blind run contamination: Redwood will perform a two-stage approach so we meet your concern:
   - Stage 1: we will run the blind dataset against the current baseline prompts (no tuning) to capture a "raw" baseline.
   - Stage 2: if you approve, we will apply a single controlled prompt-tuning pass (documented changes) and re-run to show delta. Both results will be reported; acceptance is based on the raw baseline meeting the threshold unless you opt into tuned acceptance.

2) Latency fallbacks:
   - Auto-fallback to a lower-cost/shorter-context variant when P95 spikes above 220 ms for more than 10 continuous minutes.
   - Auto-scale policy to add transient burst capacity (if reserved pool allows) and an alerting runbook for ops to execute manual scale.

3) Procurement: acknowledged; we'll attach a 1-page deliverables appendix to the MAP workbook for the PO (milestone-based invoices).

Operational checklist (to include in the MAP appendix):
- Sample ingestion owner (CareQuest) + transfer method (S3 pre-signed URLs).
- Data handling: anonymization checklist (fields to strip), encryption at rest/in transit.
- Rollback plan: revert to previous model variant + traffic split rollback within 30 minutes.
- Escalation path: contact matrix for 24/7 on-call (Redwood eng lead / CareQuest ops lead).

I'll update the MAP_v1.xlsx with a "deliverables for PO" sheet and the two-stage testing option. Mina and I can be on the call to confirm technical details.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
